title: The Man Who Declared War on Emus
sources: Australian War Memorial, 'The Great Emu War of 1932' (Major G.P.W. Meredith and the Royal Australian Artillery deployed with two Lewis guns)
National Archives of Australia, 'Emu War military operations in the Campion district'

lines.text: In nineteen thirty-two, Australia officially declared war on birds.
lines.caps: in 1932, | Australia | declared war | on birds.

lines.text: And the birds completely destroyed them.
See, twenty thousand giant emus invaded Western Australia's wheat fields,
eating all the crops and stomping fences into toothpicks.
So the Minister of Defense sent in Major Meredith,
armed with heavy automatic machine guns and ten thousand rounds.
The plan was simple: corner the flock and open fire.
Except emus can sprint forty miles an hour,
and had unexpectedly brilliant military tactics.
The moment soldiers aimed, the birds scattered into guerrilla squads,
ducking behind trees while the army's machine guns jammed.
One emu even took several hits, shrugged, and kept running.
Major Meredith lost his mind, reporting that emus were built like tanks.
After a month of chaos, the Australian army withdrew in defeat.
Proving that you should never, ever challenge a six-foot bird
to a gunfight on its home turf.
